actors.name: Supervised application tasks
actors.description: The cyclic application tasks (T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT at 10 ms, T_DIAG at 100 ms, CON-SUP-101) whose execution, timing and order the supervisor observes.

actors.name: Hardware watchdogs and reset logic
actors.description: The independent watchdog, the window watchdog and the reset flags of the platform (CON-SUP-003) that the supervisor services or reads.

actors.name: Controlled equipment
actors.description: The external equipment that receives the two control outputs and the status signal (CON-SUP-109) and that must end in a safe condition on a fault.

actors.name: Service tool
actors.description: The tool on the diagnostic serial line that receives fault reports and sends service requests (CON-SUP-007, CON-SUP-113).

actors.name: Test engineer
actors.description: The person who verifies the supervisor on host tests and the Renode simulator, including fault injection (CON-SUP-005, CON-SUP-116).

actors.name: Product owner
actors.description: The person who sets the configuration (tasks, timing, order) and the processor-time budget for the supervisor.

use_cases.title: Supervise task execution
use_cases.goal: Detect a stopped task, a late start, an overrun, and a wrong or skipped task order in a control cycle, against configured timing.

use_cases.title: Configure supervision
use_cases.goal: Set which tasks are supervised, and their timing and order, by configuration data without changing supervisor code.

use_cases.title: Service the hardware watchdogs only while healthy
use_cases.goal: Service the independent and the window watchdog only while every supervised task is healthy, so an unhandled failure ends in a hardware reset.

use_cases.title: Check memory integrity at start-up
use_cases.goal: Check that program code and configuration data are intact after a reset and before the application runs.

use_cases.title: Check program code integrity at run time
use_cases.goal: Repeat the program-code check in the background, completing a full pass in bounded time without disturbing application timing.

use_cases.title: Enter the safe state on a fault
use_cases.goal: On any detected fault, switch the control outputs off and show not-operational on the status signal within 50 ms.

use_cases.title: Recover by reset or latch the safe state
use_cases.goal: After the safe state, recover by a reset, or stay in the safe state until power-cycle when the same fault has repeated.

use_cases.title: Identify the reset cause
use_cases.goal: Classify the cause of any reset as watchdog, supervisor or power-on and make it known to the outside.

use_cases.title: Report faults on the diagnostic line
use_cases.goal: Report every detected fault on the diagnostic serial line with a fault code, the affected task or memory area, and a time stamp.

use_cases.title: Answer service requests
use_cases.goal: Let a service tool read the current supervision status and the last faults over the diagnostic serial line.

use_cases.title: Stay within the processor-time budget
use_cases.goal: Keep the supervisor's use of processor time within 10 % in normal operation.

use_cases.title: Verify the supervisor on a simulator
use_cases.goal: Test the supervisor without the real board, including injection of each fault class.

assumptions.text: The fifteen stakeholder needs STK-SUP-001..015 are the complete set of needs; the platform constraints CON-SUP-001..007 and the product-owner decisions CON-SUP-101..146 are given facts, not needs, and are cited as sources.

'Any fault above' in STK-SUP-009 covers the fault classes of STK-SUP-001, 002, 003, 007 and 008 and the configuration fault and watchdog-reset reports named in the product-owner decisions (CON-SUP-112, CON-SUP-115).
The application tasks, scheduler and board output stage outside the supervisor are provided by others; the system requirements state only what the supervisor-based controller must do at its boundary.
STK-SUP-014 and STK-SUP-015 are constraints on the product rather than behaviours; they are served by use cases UC-SUP-011 and UC-SUP-012 with analysis or test as verification.
